p: Why strip and validate required text in `__init__`?
why: Construction should either create a valid object or raise before it exists.

p: In this design, which single condition means an item is available?
why: Availability is derived from the absence of a borrower.

c: two fields always cause syntax errors
they can contradict and become two sources of truth
why: One representation prevents `available=True` while a borrower is recorded.

p: What must happen before assigning a new borrower?
why: All refusal conditions are checked before mutation.

p: An item is loaned to M014. A second loan raises ValueError. What should its borrower be afterward?
why: A rejected transition must preserve the previous valid state.

c: a condition that remains true after completed public operations
a variable that never has a name
why: The invariant guides construction and every state-changing method.

p: Which call should raise ValueError for a new available item?
why: Returning an item that is not on loan is an invalid transition.

p: Why test a rejected operation as well as a successful one?
c: rejection paths can partially corrupt state
why: Boundary bugs often appear during refusal and cleanup.

p: Which test proves preservation after double lending?
c: assert item.borrower_id == "M014" after the rejected call
why: The post-rejection state must equal the state before the refused request.
Validation before mutation prevents partial state changes.
